mina: Quick note from onboarding lab: observed generator iterator not closing reliably when cancelling parent ctx + auth retry. Repro and quick ideas below.

mina: Repro (tiny):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
_ = iter.Next()
cancel()
// sometimes iter.Next()/iter.Close hang and goroutines remain
```

jorge: Is this the pull iterator or streaming callback? backpressure differs.

mina: Pull iterator, but we also saw streaming block when consumer slow and buffer fills. Root seems to be channel sends without selecting on ctx.Done and auth refresher spawning unlinked goroutines.

rachel: Short fix: thread the caller ctx into all helper goroutines and make sends use: `select { case ch <- v: case <-ctx.Done(): return }`. That should stop leaks.

jorge: DX follow-ups: expose explicit close primitives to match Python/Node (`aclose()`/`.return()`). Proposal: iter.CloseWithTimeout(ctx,d) + iter.ForceClose(). Also add BackpressurePolicy option (Block | BufferWithTimeout | DropOldest).

rachel: Agreed. Add small quickstart snippet and a note in onboarding checklist recommending BufferWithTimeout for workshop demos until fix ships. Also add a unit that simulates slow consumer and checks for goroutine leaks across go1.20-1.22.

mina: I'll open an issue with repro + goroutine dump. jorge can take the auth refresher patch, rachel can draft the RFC/docs.

devex-bot: Issue created: DEX-8340 "go generator cancel teardown + auth-retry backpressure" (assigned to jorge) :white_check_mark:

mina: thanks! adding temporary note to quickstart so new users don't get stuck.
